outcome.technical: tools/prove-gates.py: every row now runs in a worker tree, never in the checkout. New pool section: pool_size() (the sweep's default_jobs, loaded from tools/sweep-selftests.py via _loader rather than copied, capped at the row count); run_ordered() (ThreadPoolExecutor, results in item order); open_workers() (mkdtemp under the temp root, falling back to /tmp when a .git sits above it; owner file prove-gates-pool.json with pid written before the first `git worktree add --detach HEAD`; _mirror() applies `git diff HEAD --binary` and copies `ls-files --others --exclude-standard`); close_workers() (worktree remove --force --force, prune, _output.remove_tree); reap_stale() (takes down pools whose owner pid is dead, run at the start of every run; a live owner's pool and any non-pool worktree are left alone). git runs with core.hooksPath=devnull and GIT_DIR-family vars stripped. prove() runs `sh tools/redfirst.sh ... --allow-dirty` from the worker tree (cwd=tree, the tree's own redfirst copy; redfirst.sh unchanged), worker_env() points CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/PWD at the tree, and the row's file bytes are compared before/after as a backstop (ERROR verdict + restore if a row left it mutated). _prove() runs red+allow as ONE queue then renders each half in table order. _proved() refuses rows with no worker tree (never falls back to the checkout). MARKER DECISION: main() no longer holds _suite's marker: it existed so a concurrent sweep would not read a half-mutated checkout, and the checkout is never written now; a second run is not refused either (two pools, disjoint). A pool that cannot open exits 2 (the drive reads that as a refusal); close problems go to stderr. Selftest: _changed_run fakes the pool (no worktree registered with the checkout by the suite); ch2 now asserts sorted rows + rendered table order + one pool opened and no marker; ch3 asserts no pool.
